questions.question: What is a design criterion?
choices: A restriction on available resources only
An unmeasured personal prediction
A feature or level of performance a solution should achieve
A required material in every design

questions.question: What is a design constraint?
choices: A limit such as cost, time, materials, or safety requirements
Any measured improvement
A result that must always increase
A scientific law with no practical role

questions.question: What is a prototype?
choices: A guarantee of final success
The complete finished product in every case
A list of unrelated problems
A preliminary version built to test a design

questions.question: What is iteration in design?
choices: Building one version without testing
Repeating a test-and-revision cycle
Choosing a solution only by appearance
Replacing all criteria with new units

questions.question: What is a design tradeoff?
choices: Improving one feature while accepting a disadvantage in another
A situation where every feature improves without limits
A test performed without measurements
A way to avoid all constraints

questions.question: What is optimization?
choices: Maximizing cost regardless of need
Improving performance within stated criteria and constraints
Removing every requirement
Assuming one design is best in all settings

questions.question: What is a failure point in a prototype test?
choices: A measurement that always supports the design
A reason never to test again
The name of the final product
A part or condition where performance stops meeting requirements

questions.question: Why should a problem be defined before choosing materials?
choices: Materials should be chosen before the intended use is considered
Every design problem has identical material requirements
The intended need and requirements guide useful choices
Available materials determine success without defined criteria

questions.question: Why compare several possible solutions?
choices: Different designs may meet requirements with different strengths and weaknesses
Only one solution can ever be imagined
Comparison guarantees no future failures
Every possible design has identical performance

questions.question: Why should prototypes be tested under relevant conditions?
choices: Only appearance affects real-world performance
Prototypes cannot be measured
Performance may differ from ideal conditions assumed during planning
Realistic testing removes all need for safety planning

questions.question: How can a decision matrix help compare designs?
choices: It proves all criteria are equally important
It organizes performance against agreed criteria
It replaces evidence with random choices
It guarantees every prototype passes

questions.question: Why can a lightweight bridge design require a strength tradeoff?
choices: Lower mass always guarantees greater strength
Mass and structure are unrelated to loads
All bridges have identical strength
Reducing material can change load capacity

questions.question: Why should safety be included in design evaluation?
choices: Safety matters only after a product fails
Testing eliminates all hazards permanently
Safety can be measured only by product color
A high-performing solution may still create unacceptable risks

questions.question: Why is repeated testing useful when results vary?
choices: It guarantees all trials become identical
It helps estimate reliability rather than relying on one successful trial
It makes documented methods unnecessary
It allows failed trials to be ignored

questions.question: How does engineering design differ in emphasis from scientific explanation?
choices: Engineering never uses scientific evidence
Science never uses models
Design develops solutions to needs; science investigates explanations of phenomena
Engineering avoids testing

questions.question: A device must fit in a 10 cm space and cost under $20. Which descriptions fit these requirements?
choices: Constraints on size and cost
Evidence that the prototype already works
Measurements of actual output power
Unrelated experimental results

questions.question: A filter must remove at least 90% of a test particle type. What is this requirement?
choices: A publication date
A measurable performance criterion
An uncontrolled variable
A scientific name

questions.question: Two designs meet strength requirements. One costs $15 and one $25; the budget limit is $20. Which fits the stated conditions?
choices: The $25 design
Neither design because strength is irrelevant
Both designs regardless of cost
The $15 design

questions.question: A prototype fails mainly at one joint during loading. What is a useful next step?
choices: Revise the joint and retest under comparable conditions
Ignore the joint and report only successful trials
Change the load units to make the result look larger
Declare all possible designs impossible

questions.question: One shelter design is warmer but heavier; another is lighter but colder. What should guide selection?
choices: Always choose the lighter design without considering warmth
Always choose the warmer design without considering mass
Prioritized criteria, use conditions, and acceptable tradeoffs
Assume all criteria have the same priority in every setting
